story.owner.founder: Its founder, {name} ({age}), has run it for {tenure, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.owner.heir: {name}, of the founding family's second generation, has run it for {tenure, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.owner.professional: The family has stepped back; a hired chief executive, {name}, has run it for {tenure, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.owner.sponsor: {house} bought it about {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} ago; {name} runs it.
story.owner.corporate: A non-core subsidiary of a larger group, run by {name}, who was sent in by the group.
story.owner.public: Listed. {name} runs it under the board's eye.
story.trait.single_plant: All production sits in one plant: if it stops, the company stops.
story.trait.long_term_contracts: Multi-year supply contracts with the main customers keep revenue steady.
story.trait.aging_equipment: The equipment is old; a large replacement is not far off.
story.trait.brand_strength: The name is known in the trade and earns a little more on price.
story.trait.family_workforce: Many people have been there for decades, often whole families.
story.trait.export_heavy: Much of revenue is exports, so it rides currencies and foreign demand.
story.trait.recurring_revenue: Most revenue is service contracts that bill every month.
story.trait.fragmented_market: A market of many small competitors: room to grow by buying them.
story.trait.seasonal_demand: High and low seasons are far apart; quarters swing.
story.trait.proprietary_process: A process of its own that competitors cannot easily copy.
story.trait.underinvested_sales: A small sales team: money spent on selling would show.
story.trait.regulated_customers: Customers in regulated industries: hard to win, slow to leave.
story.style.operator: {name} is an operator who watches the floor and the costs.
story.style.seller: {name} built revenue by meeting customers in person.
story.style.engineer: {name} came up through engineering and cares deeply about product and process.
story.style.financier: {name} came up through finance and reads the numbers and the cash closely.
story.style.patriarch: {name} treats the company like family and weighs who buys it as much as the price.
story.union.strong: The workforce is {union} unionized: any change to headcount starts with talks.
story.union.weak: There is hardly a union; staffing is fairly flexible.
story.trend.up: Revenue grew {cagr} a year over the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.trend.down: Revenue fell {cagr} a year over the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.trend.flat: Revenue has been flat over the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
story.teaser: Only teaser numbers so far: revenue around {revenue}, EBITDA around {ebitda}.
story.sale.retirement: The founder is nearing retirement and looking for someone to hand it to.
story.sale.succession: No child to take over, so the family chose a sale over succession.
story.sale.fund_exit: The fund that owns it is near the end of its life and selling.
story.sale.non_core: The parent wants to focus on its core and has put this up for sale.
story.sale.distress: Debt has become a burden; the sale runs under pressure from lenders.
story.sale.strategic_review: The board is reviewing options, a sale among them.
story.intent.closed: The owner says they are not selling.
story.intent.thinking: The owner has started to think they will have to sell one day.
story.intent.open: On good terms, the owner would sell.
